subject: Clarify mixed streaming vs batch rounding and bulk-discount application
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@brightcart.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing question: mixed streaming/batch rounding + discounts

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. We’re reconciling the latest invoice (attached invoice_BC-343.pdf) and have two related questions that are blocking our finance review:

1) We use the API in two modes: streaming for interactive UX and batched calls for nightly enrichment. On the invoice we see differences vs our internal token counts — can you confirm whether rounding/quantum is applied per request (streaming fragments and batch requests each rounded) or after you aggregate usage?

2) We have a committed discount in our contract (10% at SKU level). Does Redwood apply the discount to the aggregated pre-rounding token total, or to the post-rounding billed units? This matters for our forecast.

I attached a small snapshot of the lines we don’t understand. Can you point us to the exact rules and maybe provide a couple of mini-calculations with numbers similar to ours?

Thanks — can align on a quick 30-min call if easier.

Best,
Alex

BrightCart

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing question: mixed streaming/batch rounding + discounts

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear note and the invoice. Quick summary before we dig into numbers:

- We apply the per-request quantum (our "billing quantum") to each request before aggregation. In practice that means a streaming call that emits multiple partial frames is still billed against the request-level token totals after we apply the quantum to that request.
- After per-request rounding, we sum billed units across the invoice period and then apply contract-level discounts to the aggregated billed units. Finally we apply invoice-level normalization (e.g., currency rounding) to the discounted total.

I’m looping in Jordan (runtime) + Sergio (account lead) so Jordan can call out exact rounding rules and edge cases. Meanwhile, attached is a quick calc I put together to show three example scenarios (stream-heavy, batch-heavy, mixed).

Proposed next steps:
- Jordan to confirm exact quantum sizes and treatment of microfloors for heartbeat/prefix traffic.
- If the calc looks OK, we can schedule a 30-minute reconciliation.

Putting two small examples inline to keep this moving:

Example A — streaming-heavy (single interactive request):
- Raw tokens (client-side): 1,120 tokens
- Our per-request quantum: 64 tokens -> billed for the request = ceil(1120 / 64) * 64 = 1,152 tokens

Example B — batch file with 3 requests (one job):
- Raw tokens per request: 42, 85, 90 -> per-request billed units: 64, 128, 128 -> summed billed units = 320 tokens

Discount application (contract 10%):
- We sum per-request billed units across billing period (e.g., 1,152 + 320 = 1,472) then apply 10% discount = 1,324.8 -> invoice rounds currency/units per invoice policy.

Please review the attached spreadsheet and Jordan will follow up with the precise microfloor behavior.

-Kimberly

Thanks Kimberly — that helps a lot. Two follow-ups from our side:

1) In your Example A, is the quantum applied to the whole request (i.e., 1,120 tokens aggregated on server side) or do you apply quanta to each frame that the client streams? We occasionally see spikes where a single user session produces multiple separate streaming frames that total ~1,120 but are emitted in 4 frames (e.g., 280, 280, 280, 280). Will that be billed as 4 * ceil(280/64)*64 or 1 * ceil(1120/64)*64?

2) We also saw an item in the invoice flagged "microfloor credit" — can you confirm what triggers that and whether it affects the pre-discount aggregation? I attached a screenshot of the line.

If it’s easier, happy to do the 30-min call — midday PST tomorrow works for me.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing question: mixed streaming/batch rounding + discounts

Hi Alex — Jordan here (runtime/product infra). Apologies for the delay; wanted to give an exact, authoritative answer and a couple more edge-case examples.

Short answers:
1) We bill at the request boundary. If your client opens one logical request and streams frames for it, we aggregate tokens for that request and apply the quantum once. If the client issues four independent streaming requests (even if close in time) those are billed separately.

2) "Microfloor credit" is our anti-noise concession for tiny, frequent requests: we detect pathological patterns below a 16-token microfloor per request for customers on pilot tiers and may issue a nominal credit (or suppress microbilling) as a goodwill adjustment. Microfloor credits are applied after per-request rounding but before contract-level discounts (so they reduce the aggregated billed units that discounts are applied to).

Precise mechanics and examples:
- Billing quantum: default = 64 tokens (customer contract may specify alternative quantums for committed SKUs).
- Per-request billing: billed_units_request = ceil(raw_tokens_request / quantum) * quantum.
- Aggregation: billed_units_period = sum(billed_units_request for period) - microfloor_credits.
- Discounting: discounted_units = billed_units_period * (1 - discount_percent).
- Invoice normalization: final_currency = round_money(discounted_units * unit_price) per invoice currency rules.

Example C — streaming frames under one request (frames coalesced server-side):
- Frames: 280 + 280 + 280 + 280 = 1,120 raw tokens
- We see one request id -> billed = ceil(1120/64)*64 = 1152 tokens

Example D — multiple independent streaming requests (4 separate requests):
- Each frame treated as own request of 280 tokens -> per-request billed = 320 tokens each -> sum = 1,280 tokens (worse than coalesced single request).

Why this matters: some SDKs open one request per user turn and stream multiple frames for incremental updates (we treat that as one request). If you see unexpectedly higher billed units, check whether your client is creating separate request boundaries.

Edge-case: burst-prefix heartbeat (small keepalive pings)
- Heartbeat pings under 16 tokens are candidates for microflooring; if they exceed a configured pilot threshold we bill normally.

If helpful, we can:
- Share a short instrumented trace of a few sample requests (IDs) from your traffic window so you can confirm how the server grouped frames.
- Add a billing debug export to next invoice so the per-request raw vs billed units column is visible.

Attaching the public playbook excerpt for rounding/credits. Happy to hop on a call — Kimberly / Sergio to coordinate schedule.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
VP, Product, Redwood Inference
